Q: Extract substring in excel cell A:

Assuming that your output values don't contain any spaces (i.e. "A:Red B:Light Blue C:Green" would give errors), you can TEXTSPLIT the string into a table and run a VLOOKUP against it:

=VLOOKUP(B1, TEXTSPLIT(A1, ":", " "), 2, FALSE)

If your output values do contain spaces, then you will need something more involved, such as:

=LET(x, TEXTBEFORE(TEXTAFTER(A1&" ?:", B1&":"), ":"), TRIM(LEFT(x, LEN(x)-2)))

This will first extract everything after the identifier, then extract everything before the next colon from that, and drop the next identifier. It supports up to 2-letter identifiers (e.g. "A:Red B:Blue C:Orange[…]Y:Chartreuse Z:Burnt Ochre AA:Periwinkle")

Q: IJ031070: Transaction cannot proceed: STATUS_MARKED_ROLLBACK A:

In my Case, it was related to a setting in Microsoft Local DTC Properties. I had to use the value: "NT AUTHORITY\NetworkService" as the DTC Logon Account, And I had check "Network DTC Access" and "Allow Inbound" and "Allow Outbound" My own issue was because i was using XA for my transactions and the Local DTC Properties weren't setup properly. Microsoft Event Viewer was also of great help. Read up how to use it to help you track exactly what the error is. See useful links below: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows/win32/msdtc-service-run-under-networkservice-account

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/performance/view-the-windows-application-log-windows-10?view=sql-server-ver16

Q: Parenting and deparenting game objects A:

I haven't wrote any climbing mechanic but manipulating parenting seems bug prone to me.

Here is how I'll handle it :

  • Define the center point of your character while climbing (Let's say the belly)
  • When you hit a climbable collider stop the gravity and clear all forces (optionally store the forces so that you can use them the way you want, that's useful for the polish step)
  • Raycast from your belly (the center point you defined) toward the climbableCollider and use the contact to correcly set the position and rotation of the character.
  • Change an enum/boolean somewhere in your code so that now you use the climbing character movement function you wrote.

Press "space" to get off the climbing mode while adding ForceImpulse to your character to get off the wall

Q: git repository clone failed. Connection Reset A:

Increase Preferences/Version Control/Git/Remote Connections/Connection timeout

Helps when poorly implemented HTTPS server needs to do a lot of processing.

Q: How do I implement a cylindrical grid for a 3D plot? A:

I'm trying to achieve something similar to .

Yes, it has foreshortening, but I think it represents the trajectory better than

For many cases I like the idea of using color to represent, but here I think the line representing the trajectory is too thin for the color to clearly represent the information.

(first one is same as this plot at Early Space Missions, ESS 265, UCLA and very similar to a plot at About Voyager's Flight. The other plot is Figure 2 of The Voyager 2 encounter with Uranus)

Neither of these plots use a polar grid but they both attempt to communicate radial distance. I really think the polar grid would be more useful than the rectangular grid -- I don't think anyone is trying any useful information from a rectangular grid in a plot like this.
